Oval Face Shape

By AI Rate Face · Updated September 8, 2026 · Reference choices

An oval contour is longer than it is wide, with the widest point at the cheekbones and a gentle taper toward a rounded chin. It sits in the middle of the seven profiles, which is why styling guides so often treat it as the default — not because it is better, but because it is the least directional, so fewer choices are working against a strong feature.

Check your own shape free →

Moderately long, with the forehead a little wider than the jaw and a softly rounded chin.

How to tell if your face is oval

These visual cues can be checked in a mirror. If several do not fit, compare the neighbouring profiles below.

  • 01

    Face length is noticeably greater than cheek width — roughly one and a half times.

  • 02

    The forehead is slightly wider than the jaw, but the difference is modest rather than dramatic.

  • 03

    The jaw curves rather than turning a corner, and the chin is rounded instead of pointed or flat.

  • 04

    No single region — forehead, cheekbones or jaw — clearly dominates the outline.

What the detector matches you against

These are the exact reference values the oval profile uses. Your photo is scored against all seven profiles on these five measurements, and the closest ones are returned as percentages rather than a single label.

MeasurementOval referenceWhat it means
Face length / cheek width1.44Visible upper-face landmark to chin, divided by cheek-level landmark width; the model does not detect the exact hairline.
Forehead / cheek width0.82Temple-level width as a share of cheek width.
Jaw / cheek width0.78Jaw-corner width as a share of cheek width.
Jaw corner angle150°Higher is a softer, more curved corner; lower is a squarer one.
Chin taper angle104°Higher is a broader chin; lower is a more pointed one.

These reference values are hand-set design choices, not population averages fitted to a labelled dataset. They define what this tool means by oval; another calculator using different landmarks will place the boundaries elsewhere.

If oval does not feel right

Oblong

Both taper the same way; oblong is simply longer. If your face length is more than about 1.6× your cheek width, the oblong profile fits better.

Read the oblong guide →

Diamond

A diamond has a narrower forehead relative to the cheekbones. If your temples are clearly narrower than your cheekbones, the diamond profile is closer.

Read the diamond guide →

What tends to suit a oval face

These are visual-balance conventions, not rules. They describe where volume, width or a line is usually placed to work with or against the natural contour — and either direction is a valid choice.

Hairstyles

  • •Most lengths work; preserve the natural outline instead of hiding it.
  • •Try a soft side part or textured layers for movement.
  • •Use fringe only if it suits your hair texture and routine.
Run the hairstyle finder →

Glasses

  • •Try frames as wide as, or slightly wider than, the cheek contour.
  • •Rectangular, round and softly geometric shapes can all work.
  • •Check bridge fit and pupil alignment before choosing by shape.
Run the glasses finder →

Beard shapes

  • •Most beard lengths work; a moderate, evenly trimmed shape preserves the existing taper.
  • •A very long or heavily squared beard will read as oblong, which changes the outline rather than following it.
  • •Keep the cheek line natural — a severely straight line can flatten the curve of the contour.

Contour and makeup

  • •Little contouring is needed for balance; most people place a soft blush along the cheekbone.
  • •If you want more structure, a light touch under the cheekbone adds definition without narrowing the face.
  • •Brow shape has more visual effect here than contour does, because nothing else is competing for attention.

Earrings, necklines and hats

  • •Most earring shapes work; studs, drops and hoops all sit comfortably against the outline.
  • •Both crew and V necklines suit this profile — the choice is about the neck and shoulders, not the face.
  • •Hat brims of any width are workable; a medium brim keeps the proportions as they are.

About the oval shape

Measure your own face free →
Is an oval face the best face shape?+

No. Oval is described as versatile because it is the least directional of the seven, so fewer styling choices push against it. Versatile is a practical description, not a ranking, and no measured contour is objectively more attractive than another.

How do I know if my face is oval and not oblong?+

Length. Both taper toward the chin in the same way, so the deciding measurement is face length divided by cheek width — around 1.44 leans oval, around 1.64 leans oblong.
